fullPassage:
[1번] Clever and cute, cats are beloved by people around the world. That's why, in the 1960s, the CIA decided they would make perfect spies. It was believed that nobody would suspect a cat of working for the government. After choosing a female cat, doctors surgically placed a tiny transmitter in her chest, along with a microphone in her ear and an antenna running along her backbone. Performing the operation was not that hard. However, training the cat proved to be quite difficult because they are such stubborn animals. Finally, after five years of training, the CIA concluded their animal agent was ready. So, they sent her to record a conversation between two men from the Soviet Union. Sadly, the cat was hit by a passing taxi after taking only a few steps. As a result of this unsuccessful experiment, the idea of using cats was abandoned.

[2번] One tradition found in many ancient cultures is burying the dead with things they might need in the afterlife, such as food, weapons, and clothing. Archaeologists in western Norway, however, have found an unexpected item in a grave that dates back to the Early Iron Age — a board game. The board itself was missing, but the archaeologists found dice and game pieces. They believe that the board game was an indication that the dead person was wealthy. This is because board games were a symbol of social status and power in ancient civilizations. Only someone who was educated and didn't need to work could spend time playing them. The likely purpose of burying the board game was to provide the dead person with entertainment in the next world.

[3번] If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making impulsive purchases.

[4번] Triboulet was born in France in the 15th century. His body looked different from those of other people. He had short, crooked legs and long arms. People teased him about how he looked, but Triboulet just made it part of his sense of humor. He was so funny that it was his job to make the king laugh. But Triboulet was not just funny. He was also very bold. One day, Triboulet found himself in serious trouble. He had decided to slap the backside of the king. The king didn't consider it funny and demanded an apology. Triboulet apologized by saying, "I'm sorry. I didn't recognize you! I thought you were the queen!" The king found this even less amusing. He decided to put him to death. He allowed Triboulet to choose how he would die. Triboulet immediately replied, "I choose to die of old age." The king liked this clever answer, so he called off the execution.

[5번] Today, with the advent of the internet and new technology for editing digital material, more people than ever before can produce artistic creations and share them with the world. Many critics, though, have expressed concern that this is causing us to lose our sense of what makes truly great art. Great art challenges our perceptions of the world and forever changes our thoughts and feelings. Artists ought to remember that new technologies are nothing more than tools that can be used in the creative process. In other words, the goal of the modern artist should not be simply to utilize technology for its own sake. Rather, it should be to produce unique creations that will allow the public to have new, eye-opening experiences.

[6번] When Harriet Beecher Stowe published the novel Uncle Tom's Cabin in 1852, it had a significant effect on the United States. At that time, slavery was still legal in the southern part of the country. The book's anti-slavery message made people in the Northern states begin to realize just how bad slavery was. This was partly because Stowe wrote in a very personal, informal style that enabled readers to empathize with the slaves in her novel. Stowe's novel had a stronger effect than newspaper articles and political speeches. It inspired many ordinary Americans to believe that they could help make the world a better place. Nine years after Uncle Tom's Cabin was published, the American Civil War began, which eventually led to the end of slavery.

[7번] Have you ever wanted to say something but found yourself struggling to remember the correct word? This is called the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon. There are several different things that can cause it. In some cases, it happens because you feel exhausted. In other cases, it is caused by having a weak memory of the missing information. No matter what the cause is, you shouldn't struggle to remember the desired information, as this can make it more difficult to recall in the future. A better way of resolving the situation is to simply look it up online. Once you've found the word, you can break the cycle by repeating the word over and over, either aloud or silently. This creates something called a procedural memory, which will lower the chances of the word being forgotten again.

[8번] Voter advice applications, sometimes referred to as VAAs, are short online quizzes. Voters who take them have their opinions on social issues matched to the policies of political parties. VAAs get users engaged in the political process by encouraging them to do further research on these policies and participate in elections more. They also help users decide on who they should vote for. What's more, most VAAs collect and save data anonymously, allowing it to be used to create informative reports about the country's political situation. Currently, VAAs are popular in a number of European countries, including the Netherlands, Germany, and Finland. They are expected to become more widely used around the world in the near future.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) perfect=완벽한 / useless=쓸모없는 (B) concluded=결론지었다 / doubted=의심했다 (C) ready=준비된 / unprepared=준비되지 않은
det.analysis:
① useless: 고양이가 '쓸모없는' 스파이가 될 것? CIA가 완벽한(perfect) 스파이로 여긴 문맥과 반대
② perfect—concluded—ready: 완벽한 스파이가 되고, CIA가 준비됐다고 결론짓고, 요원이 준비된 상태 ←정답
③ doubted/unprepared: '의심했다'/'준비 안 됨'은 훈련 완료 후 파견한 흐름과 반대
④ 세 자리 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 완벽한(perfect) 스파이 → 5년 훈련 후 결론지음(concluded) → 준비됨(ready)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) advent=출현 / decline=쇠퇴 (B) remember=기억하다 / forget=잊다 (C) utilize=활용하다 / ignore=무시하다

questions.passage: One tradition found in many ancient cultures is burying the dead with things they might need in the __________, such as food, weapons, and clothing. Archaeologists in western Norway, however, have found an unexpected item in a grave that dates back to the Early Iron Age — a board game. The board itself was missing, but the archaeologists found dice and game pieces. They believe that the board game was an indication that the dead person was wealthy. This is because board games were a symbol of social status and power in ancient civilizations. Only someone who was educated and didn't need to work could spend time playing them. The likely purpose of burying the board game was to provide the dead person with entertainment in the next world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: future city=미래 도시 / daily market=일상 시장 / modern world=현대 세계 / afterlife=사후 세계
det.analysis:
① future city: 죽은 자가 미래 도시에서? 문맥 부적절
② daily market: 일상 시장에서 필요? 부적절
③ modern world: 고대 문화 이야기와 안 맞음
④ afterlife: 죽은 자를 매장하며 넣는 것은 사후 세계에서 필요한 물건 ←정답
det.tip: burying the dead(죽은 자 매장) + 뒤에 next world(다음 세계) 반복 → afterlife(사후 세계)

questions.passage: If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it (A)[difficult / easy] to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become (B)[exhausted / energized] from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making (C)[rational / impulsive] purchases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) difficult=어려운 / easy=쉬운 (B) exhausted=지친 / energized=활력 넘치는 (C) impulsive=충동적인 / rational=이성적인
det.analysis:
① easy: 게임 환경은 시간 파악을 '어렵게' 만든다 → difficult
② difficult—exhausted—impulsive: 시간 파악이 어렵고, 뇌가 지치며, 충동 구매로 이어짐 ←정답
③ energized/rational: 결정을 많이 해 '지치고' '충동적'이 됨. 반대
④ 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 게임/쇼핑몰이 시간 인식을 흐트러뜨림 → difficult, exhausted, impulsive의 부정적 흐름

questions.passage: Triboulet was born in France in the 15th century. His body looked ①<u>different</u> from those of other people. He had short, crooked legs and long arms. People ②<u>teased</u> him about how he looked, but Triboulet just made it part of his sense of humor. He was so funny that it was his job to make the king ③<u>laugh</u>. But Triboulet was not just funny. He was also very ④<u>timid</u>. One day, Triboulet found himself in serious trouble. He had decided to slap the backside of the king. The king didn't consider it funny and demanded an apology. Triboulet apologized by saying, "I'm sorry. I didn't recognize you! I thought you were the queen!" The king found this even less amusing. He decided to put him to death. He allowed Triboulet to choose how he would die. Triboulet immediately replied, "I choose to die of old age." The king liked this clever answer, so he called off the execution.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① different=다른 ② teased=놀렸다 ③ laugh=웃다 ④ bold→timid (부적절)
det.analysis:
① different: 그의 몸은 다른 사람들과 달라 보였다 — 적절
② teased: 사람들이 그를 놀렸다 — 적절
③ laugh: 왕을 웃기는 것이 그의 일이었다 — 적절
④ timid: 소심한(timid) 사람이 왕의 엉덩이를 때린다? 대담한(bold)이 원문 ←정답
det.tip: 왕의 엉덩이를 때릴 정도면 대담한(bold) 것. timid(소심한)는 정반대

questions.passage: Today, with the advent of the internet and new technology for editing digital material, more people than ever before can produce (A)[artistic / destructive] creations and share them with the world. Many critics, though, have expressed concern that this is causing us to lose our sense of what makes truly great art. Great art (B)[confirms / challenges] our perceptions of the world and forever changes our thoughts and feelings. Artists ought to remember that new technologies are nothing more than tools that can be used in the creative process. In other words, the goal of the modern artist should not be simply to utilize technology for its own sake. Rather, it should be to produce (C)[unique / typical] creations that will allow the public to have new, eye-opening experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) artistic=예술적인 / destructive=파괴적인 (B) challenges=이의를 제기하다 / confirms=확인해주다 (C) unique=독특한 / typical=전형적인
det.analysis:
① artistic — challenges — unique: 사람들이 예술적(artistic) 창작물을 만들고, 위대한 예술은 인식에 이의를 제기하며(challenges), 예술가는 독특한(unique) 창작물을 만들어야 한다 ←정답
② destructive — confirms — typical: 파괴적/확인/전형적 모두 문맥과 반대
③ artistic — confirms — typical: (B) 인식을 '확인해주다'는 뒤의 '생각을 바꾼다'와 모순, (C) 전형적은 '새로운 경험'과 모순
④ destructive — challenges — unique: (A) 파괴적 창작물은 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 위대한 예술은 인식에 도전(challenges)하고 독특한(unique) 창작물을 만든다는 흐름

questions.passage: It was believed that nobody would suspect a cat of __________ (work) for the government.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: work(동사: 일하다) → working(동명사). 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 온다
det.analysis: 전치사 of 다음에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로 work를 working으로 바꾼다. 'suspect A of -ing'은 'A가 ~한다고 의심하다'라는 표현이다
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤 → 동명사(-ing). suspect ~ of working

questions.passage: This is because board games were a symbol of social status and power in ancient civilizations. Only someone who was __________ (educate) and didn't need to work could spend time playing them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: educate(교육하다) → educated(교육받은). be동사 + 과거분사 수동/형용사 형태
det.analysis: educate를 과거분사 educated로 변환. 'someone who was educated'는 '교육받은 사람'을 뜻하는 수동 표현 — 주어가 교육을 '받는' 대상이므로 be + p.p.
det.tip: was _____ → 수동/상태 (be + p.p.) → educated(교육받은)

questions.passage: We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become __________ (exhaust) from making too many decisions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: exhaust(동사: 지치게 하다) → exhausted(과거분사: 지친). become + p.p. 형태로 상태를 나타냄
det.analysis: exhaust를 과거분사 exhausted로 변환. 'become exhausted'=지치게 되다. 사람·뇌가 '지쳐지는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 필요
det.tip: become + 형용사/과거분사. 뇌가 '지친' 상태 → exhausted

questions.passage: The king demanded an apology. Triboulet apologized by __________ (say), "I'm sorry. I didn't recognize you!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: say(동사: 말하다) → saying(동명사). 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)
det.analysis: say를 동명사 saying으로 변환. 'apologized by saying'=말함으로써 사과했다 — 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 함
det.tip: 전치사(by) + 동명사(-ing). by saying=말함으로써

questions.passage: Great art challenges our perceptions of the world and forever __________ (change) our thoughts and feelings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: change(동사: 바꾸다) → changes. 주어 Great art가 3인칭 단수이고 현재시제이므로 동사에 -s
det.analysis: 주어 'Great art'는 3인칭 단수예요. 현재시제 문장이라 동사 change에 -s를 붙여 changes로 써요. 앞의 challenges와 and로 연결된 병렬 구조라 형태도 맞춰요
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(Great art) + 현재시제 → 동사 + s → changes
